exclusions.alternative_reading: HB 4168 set the single standard deduction at $15,750 'subject to subsection H', and subsection H requires the department to adjust it 'in the same manner in which the federal basic standard deduction is adjusted for inflation pursuant to section 63'. The federal basic standard deduction starts from the same $15,750 and is $16,100 for 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32), so Arizona's 2026 single deduction is $16,100.
exclusions.defect: policyengine-us puts the Arizona standard deduction's uprating on the parent parameter node, which policyengine-core does not propagate to the filing-status children, so the 2025 amount ($15,750 single) carries into 2026 unindexed

exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by the reference adversary (runs/claude/cases/us__scenario_025__state_income_tax_before_refundable_credits) and verified independently on 2026-10-06 (verification/independent/oh_025.md). Alternative value: hand computation from the engine's Ohio AGI, exemptions, rate schedule and retirement income credit (verification/independent/oh_025.md section 4).
exclusions.alternative_reading: R.C. 5747.01(A)(10)(b) deducts unreimbursed medical care above 7.5% of federal AGI, and (A)(10)(c) defines medical care by IRC 213(d), which includes insurance premiums. The head's $6,500 of after-tax non-employer premiums plus $800 of other medical expenses ($7,300) exceed 7.5% of federal AGI ($7,119.40) by $180.60.
exclusions.defect: policyengine-us counts health insurance premiums toward Ohio's 7.5%-of-federal-AGI medical deduction only when the person is Medicare-eligible AND has no employer-paid plan, where Ohio's worksheet line 3 reads 'Medicare or an employer-paid health care plan', so a non-Medicare filer with employer coverage gets no premium credit

exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by the reference adversary (runs/claude/cases/us__scenario_082__state_refundable_credits) and verified independently on 2026-10-06 (verification/independent/ny_082.md). Alternative value: hand computation from the engine's New York AGI and Empire State child credit (verification/independent/ny_082.md section 3).
exclusions.alternative_reading: Tax Law 606(c-2) gives, for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, a refundable credit of the applicable percentage (55%, less 0.00025 percentage points per dollar of New York AGI above $15,000, floor 4%) of qualifying expenses up to $3,000 for one child. At New York AGI of $117,585.15 that is 29.3537% of $3,000 = $880.61, plus the $307 Empire State child credit.
exclusions.defect: policyengine-us computes New York's 2026 child and dependent care credit with the pre-2026 formula (a percentage of the federal credit), which L.2026 ch. 59 limited to tax years beginning before 2026 and replaced with the refundable 606(c-2) credit on qualifying expenses

regenerations.basis: Tax Law 606(c-2) gives, for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, a refundable credit of the applicable percentage (55%, less 0.00025 percentage points per dollar of New York AGI above $15,000, floor 4%) of qualifying expenses up to $3,000 for one child. At New York AGI of $117,585.15 that is 29.3537% of $3,000 = $880.61, plus the $307 Empire State child credit.
